compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`rebar-journal-usage-high` (`journal_used_percent > 85`, 300/6/6, `Maximum`) has been in ALARM since 2026-10-09 22:36 PDT. Over the last 5 days every 5-minute sample read 99.4-101.2% of the 3 GiB ceiling. The ceiling is in force: `rebar-journal-cap-not-in-effect` is OK, the drop-in on the host sets `SystemMaxUse=3221225472`, journald logs routine rotation, and root disk is at 35%. `SystemMaxUse` is a target journald fills to and then holds, so a threshold below 100 fires permanently in steady state and carries no signal. Found by the 2026-11-02 read-only ops sweep (session a85e3cd3).

## Root cause
The 85 threshold was set before the journal had filled (it grew about 25 MB/day from 2026-09-29 until it reached the ceiling around 2026-10-25). `infra/scripts/journald-cap.sh:20-21` already documents the bound: only archived files are vacuumed, so usage can exceed the ceiling by up to one active file (`SystemMaxFileSize`, default 1/8), and the honest worst case is 9/8 of the ceiling, i.e. 112.5%. `observability.sh` `pct_of_cap` is intentionally unclamped (bug b380), so readings above 112 are publishable.

## Approach
Re-threshold, do not add a mechanism. Set `threshold = 112` (`GreaterThanThreshold`) on `journal_usage_high` in `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:562`, so the alarm fires only when usage exceeds journald's documented worst case: the condition in which journald is NOT vacuuming (rotation or vacuum failure). Rationale: "cap not in force" is already covered by `rebar-journal-cap-not-in-effect` (`journal_cap_in_effect < 1`), and disk headroom by `rebar-root-disk-pressure`. Rejected: a new rotation-failure metric parsed from the journal (adds a mechanism the ratchet must justify while the reading already carries the signal); deleting the alarm (loses vacuum-failure detection). Window shape 300/6/6/breaching is unchanged.

Rewrite the alarm description (kept within the 1024-byte limit pinned by `tests/unit/test_alarm_description_byte_limit.py`) to say the journal normally sits at ~100% and the alarm means usage is past 9/8 of the ceiling. Update the "Which alarm fired?" row for `rebar-journal-usage-high` in `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` (~line 1072). Correct `infra/runbooks/alarm-window-tuning.md` where it states every 85% threshold measures the right quantity (line ~348), naming this exception and its measured evidence.

## Scope
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf` — `journal_usage_high` threshold and description.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — journal "Which alarm fired?" row and steady-state note.
- `infra/runbooks/alarm-window-tuning.md` — correct the 2026-09-05 "no threshold is wrong" claim for this alarm.
- `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` — new test pinning the threshold to the journald worst case.
Out of scope: `journald-cap.sh`, `observability.sh`, the ceiling value, the window shape.

## Testing
Add `test_journal_usage_alarm_fires_only_past_journald_worst_case` to `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`, parsing the `journal_usage_high` block with the file's existing `_alarm_blocks()`/`_quoted_attr` masking parser. It asserts:
- the threshold is at least 112.5 minus rounding, i.e. `>= 112`, so 9/8 of the ceiling never pages;
- the threshold is below 125, so a vacuum failure that adds 1/8 more still pages (failure edge);
- the comparison is `GreaterThanThreshold`.
It must fail on the current tree (threshold 85) before the change, and pass after. The existing byte-limit, window-tuning, and missing-data tests must stay green.

## Deploy
Terraform here is applied only by an operator; autodeploy does not run it. After merge the ticket stays in_progress with the exact operator command (`cd infra/terraform && AWS_PROFILE=frontier terraform plan` then `apply`), and the expected plan diff (one in-place update of `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.journal_usage_high`: threshold 85 -> 112 plus description).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1 — `journal_usage_high` declares `threshold = 112` with `GreaterThanThreshold`; verified by the new test, which fails at threshold 85.
- [x] AC2 — the alarm description states steady state sits near 100% and the alarm means usage past 9/8 of the ceiling; it stays within 1024 bytes, verified by `tests/unit/test_alarm_description_byte_limit.py`.
- [x] AC3 — `review-bot-ops.md` and `alarm-window-tuning.md` describe the new threshold and its rationale; verified by reading the merged diff.
- [x] AC4 — targeted tests, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `terraform fmt -check` / `validate` pass; the change lands through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
- [x] AC5 [non-codebase] — after the operator apply, `rebar-journal-usage-high` is OK with the journal at its steady ~100%, verified read-only with `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --profile frontier`.
  provenance: environment=production AWS account 896586841071 us-east-1; principal=operator session via AWS_PROFILE=frontier; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — 2026-11-04 terraform apply of the reviewed plan (journal_usage_high threshold 85 -> 112, applied with the alchemic-ornate-eider changes; post-apply plan empty); aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --profile frontier shows rebar-journal-usage-high OK at 12:14 PST with journal_used_percent steady at 101%.
